A1.justification: Despite retitling and extensive revision, both PDFs describe the same self-distillation and partial-label learning research. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures provide sufficient readable evidence for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical simulations, synthetic-data experiments and CIFAR-10/100 classification results, including appendix experiments varying regularization.

after.justification: v2 reports original numerical simulations and experiments on six image datasets, including prediction-clustering analyses, candidate-label ablations and ViT-B experiments.

M1.justification: The equal-weight top-two label refinement rule is retained, but v2 Appendix E.3 specifies generalized cross-entropy with q=0.7 for PLL training, replacing the cross-entropy specified in v1. This substantively changes the implemented student's training objective, although v2's theoretical PLL objective remains cross-entropy.

E1.justification: Real-data evaluation changes from CIFAR-10/100 to CIFAR-100, Caltech-101/256, Flowers-102, Food-101 and StanfordCars; CIFAR-10 is removed. v2 also adds corruption restricted to inferred superclasses alongside the retained symmetric and asymmetric corruption scenarios.

E2.justification: The teacher and standard multi-round self-distillation comparison families remain. v2 Figure 12 adds evaluated top-3, top-4, top-5 and top-10 partial-label variants as comparators to the proposed top-two variant.

E3.justification: For CIFAR-100, the main weight decay changes from 2×10^-7 to 5×10^-5. v2 expands the learning-rate grid and corruption-rate grid, evaluates four rather than three student rounds, and introduces ViT-B settings. It replaces v1's Gaussian-feature training experiment with revised numerical Gram-matrix simulations and specifies new dataset protocols, including Caltech 80:20 splits and swapped Flowers-102 training/test sets.

E4.justification: v2 adds candidate-set-size ablations, ViT-B backbone checks and a four-class CIFAR-100 prediction-clustering analysis (Section 6 and Appendices G–H). Feature-correlation validation expands to hierarchical clustering and superclass statistics across six datasets. Regularization sensitivity and softmax-approximation checks are retained but revised.

E5.justification: Both versions report three repeated runs and numerical results with ± summaries. v2 newly identifies seeds 0, 1 and 2, and Figure 3b adds explicitly defined ±1 standard-deviation bands for softmax-output trajectories. The reported number of repeated runs does not increase.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and expanded. At 80% symmetric CIFAR-100 corruption, PLL accuracy is 47.46±0.44% in v1 Table 1 and 56.21±0.18% in v2 Table 11; changed regularization and PLL loss prevent interpreting this as a matched-setting gain. v2 adds superclass, new-dataset, candidate-size and ViT results, while removing CIFAR-10 results.

T1.justification: v1's class-correlation-dependent output derivation becomes a general Gram-matrix result in v2 Theorem 3.1, still under softmax linearization. v2 adds superclass correlation models and corresponding noise guarantees, with an explicit restriction against cross-superclass corruption. Appendices J and K add derivations for two superclass models and the evolving-feature extension in Corollary C.1.

C1.justification: The central claims about label averaging, noise-dependent accuracy guarantees and top-two PLL benefits remain. v2 additionally foregrounds computational savings from single-round PLL and claims a conditional connection to evolving features. Fixed-feature linear probing receives stronger emphasis, but was already v1's setting.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning softmax linearization, structured correlations and fixed features. Whereas v1 says the correlation assumption can be relaxed to an expectation, v2 Appendix B identifies that relaxation as future work. It also develops explanations of the candidate-set confidence tradeoff and why stronger feature correlations can reduce the required distillation rounds.

D1.justification: v2 adds numerical-solver pseudocode, dataset preparation and split instructions, superclass construction information and the GCE parameter. It documents revised hyperparameters and changes the reported hardware from GeForce 3090 GPUs to multiple RTX A6000 GPUs. The detailed Gaussian-feature generation recipe from v1 is removed with that experiment.

R1.justification: v2 substantially refocuses positioning around linear probing with foundation-model features and develops an explicit relationship to Allen-Zhu and Li's feature-learning explanation. It adds foundation-model, perturbation-theory, ViT and GCE references, while removing the noisy-PLL discussion and its associated references, including Lian et al., Xu et al. and PiCO+.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, and the abstract, introduction and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten. v2 introduces an overview with informal theorem statements, separates the principal results into dedicated sections, integrates related work into the introduction and reorganizes the appendices around limitations, extensions, experiments and proofs.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR layout and substantially redesigns the evidence presentation. Main benchmark reporting shifts from accuracy tables to gain bar charts, with detailed tables concentrated in Appendix M. Theoretical panels are reorganized and redrawn, and new prediction scatterplots, expanded correlation heatmaps, ablation charts and hierarchical-clustering diagrams are added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the paper through a broader Gram-matrix analysis and targeted tests of the mechanism, candidate-label choice and backbone dependence, addressing important gaps in v1's validation. Explicit limitations and numerical-solver documentation also improve assessability. The switch to GCE creates a mismatch with the CE-based PLL theory, but the broader analysis and stronger empirical scrutiny support a substantial net improvement.
